title: HLC receive() accepts arbitrarily far-future timestamps from peers
description: hlc.rs: receive() computes new_wall = self.last.wall_ms.max(observed.wall_ms).max(now_ms) with no bounds check on observed. A malicious or misconfigured peer sending wall_ms 100s in the future jumps the local HLC forward. Subsequent send() calls produce timestamps 100s in the future until wall clock catches up. K&D 2014 recommends a max_clock_skew bound (typically 300ms–5s). Fix: add a configurable max_clock_skew parameter; reject or cap observed timestamps beyond it.
design: Decision: reject (not cap) observations beyond the skew bound. Capping produces a silently wrong timestamp; rejecting makes the problem visible and forces operators to fix clock sync. Config: max_clock_skew_ms in [peering] section, default 5000ms. On exceed: return Err from receive(), caller drops the message and increments a hlc_clock_skew_rejections_total counter. Configurable so lab environments with mocked clocks can set a larger value.
